name: The Goethe Palm
species: European Fan Palm / Saint Peter's Palm (Chamaerops humilis)

location.address: Orto Botanico di Padova, Via Orto Botanico 15, 35123 Padova
location.neighbourhood: Orto Botanico (UNESCO World Heritage botanical garden, founded 1545)

verified_sources: https://ilregistrodeglialberi.it/3248-palma-di-goethe-palma-di-san-pietro-padova-pd-veneto
Italian national register of monumental trees (MASAF), 'Palma di San Pietro', girth 4.5 m, coordinates 45.39943,11.88105 (matches RAMI to within 15 m)
access: Paid entry (Orto Botanico admission ticket required; exact current price not verified this pass)
transport: ~1.9 km / roughly 25-30 min walk from Padova railway station; nearest bus/tram stop not verified this pass
verify_notes: One of the first plants set in the ground when the Orto Botanico was laid out, historically dated to 1585 by the garden's own records (RAMI: 'una delle prime piante messe a dimora nel 1585 pochi anni dopo da quando fu realizzato l'Orto Botanico'). Health status 'Buona' (good) per RAMI, last updated 25/07/2026. It is a polycormic clump of roughly 25 stems, each about 50 cm in girth, kept inside a purpose-built glass enclosure (the Ortus Sphaericus / octagonal greenhouse) to protect it from frost. Named for Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, who saw it on his 1786 Italian journey and wrote about it in his botanical work on plant metamorphosis; a descriptive panel at the tree tells this story. Two register names for one tree: MASAF calls it 'Palma di San Pietro', RAMI's page title is 'Palma di Goethe / Palma di San Pietro' -- same specimen, coordinates match within 15 metres. Good story hook: a single dwarf palm credited with helping inspire Goethe's theory of plant metamorphosis.

name: The Oriental Plane of the Orto Botanico

location.address: Orto Botanico di Padova, Via Orto Botanico 15, 35123 Padova

verified_sources: https://ilregistrodeglialberi.it/3247-platano-orientale-dellorto-botanico-platano-orientale-padova-pd-veneto

Independent corroboration via web search of Italian travel/garden-history sources describing the same tree, planted 1680, hollow trunk from a lightning strike, still living (searched 2026-08-06; multiple independent Italian tourism/garden pages, titles not individually re-verified against RAMI age math but agreeing on the 1680 planting date and lightning-hollowed trunk)
access: Paid entry (Orto Botanico admission ticket required)
transport: ~1.9 km / roughly 25-30 min walk from Padova railway station; nearest bus/tram stop not verified this pass
verify_notes: RAMI dates planting to 1680 per the garden's own visitor leaflet, giving an age of 346 years as of the 25/07/2026 update. Species is genuinely uncommon in Italy (Platanus orientalis is only considered native in small pockets of Calabria and Sicily; almost everything called 'plane tree' elsewhere is the hybrid Platanus x hispanica/acerifolia), which is worth stating clearly so it is not confused with the common London Plane entries elsewhere in this city. Trunk is hollow from the base up after a lightning strike but the tree still leafs out normally, conduction tissue running through the outer wood. Girth 6.2 m, height ~24.8 m per RAMI's 2021 measurement. Health 'Buona'. Flagged only because the second source is a web-search corroboration of general facts rather than a second named register/document; worth a stronger citation (e.g. the university's own Orto Botanico website) before this ships if the writer wants belt and braces, but the two sources agree independently on the same distinctive facts (1680, lightning-hollowed, still alive), which is a low-fabrication-risk profile.

name: The Grafted Ginkgo of the Orto Botanico

location.address: Orto Botanico di Padova, Via Orto Botanico 15, 35123 Padova

verified_sources: https://ilregistrodeglialberi.it/3251-ginkgo-padova-pd-veneto
Independent corroboration via web search of Italian/English garden-history sources describing the same 1750 planting as among the first ginkgo trees introduced to Italy (searched 2026-08-06)
access: Paid entry (Orto Botanico admission ticket required)
transport: ~1.9 km / roughly 25-30 min walk from Padova railway station; nearest bus/tram stop not verified this pass
verify_notes: Planted 1750 as a male ginkgo, one of the first of the species brought to Italy (RAMI says possibly the first in Italy, and the second in Europe after Utrecht's 1727 tree). The genuinely good story: in the mid-19th century a female branch was grafted onto this male tree, so it is one of very few ginkgos anywhere that both sheds pollen and bears the foul-smelling fruit, on the same trunk. Health 'Sufficiente' (adequate, not great) per RAMI's 25/07/2026 update; girth ~4.0 m, height ~17-20 m. Note there is a second, younger, ungrafted-story ginkgo in the same garden ('Ginko dell'Orto Botanico n. 2', RAMI id 14476, coords 45.399534,11.881069, no age on record) which is NOT this tree and was not separately verified or delivered this pass; leave as a lead if the writer wants a second ginkgo.
